Two-level mediation (1-1-1)

Source: vignettes/articles/model-twolevel.qmd

Models › Clusters and latent variables › Two-level mediation (1-1-1)

Treatment, mediator and outcome are all measured on the same level-1 units (students, patients, days) nested in clusters (schools, clinics, people), and you want the indirect effect at the within level and at the between level. Part of the Models collection.

Experimental. The two-level API (TwoLevelMediationData, extract_mediation() on two-level fits, fit_sem(cluster = ), nie(level = ), twolevel_statistic()) may change in a later release without the usual deprecation period.

Structure X, M and Y on level-1 units, with a within part and a between (cluster) part each (a “1-1-1” design)
Class returned TwoLevelMediationData
Indirect effect \(a_w b_w\) at the within level and \(a_b b_b\) at the between level; their difference is a descriptive contrast
Route extract_mediation() on a two-level lavaan fit (level: blocks, cluster =), or on a two-level fit from medfit’s sem engine, fit_sem(model, data, cluster = ) (The sem engine route)
Needs lavaan (Suggests) for the lavaan route; nothing extra for the sem engine
Availability lavaan route: version 0.17.0; sem engine route: version 0.20.0 (both experimental)

If the treatment is assigned to whole clusters (a 2-1-1 design), use the cluster-randomized page instead. If you have a single-level fit that only sets cluster = for robust standard errors, nothing changes: it still extracts as a MediationData.

What is estimated

lavaan’s two-level model splits each variable into a within part (a unit’s deviation from its cluster) and a between part (the cluster’s own level, a latent cluster mean). The same three regressions, M on X, Y on M and X, are fitted at both levels. medfit reads the six slopes and their joint covariance from the fit and reports, per level,

  • the indirect effect NIE = \(a \, b\), the direct effect NDE = \(c'\) and the total effect TE = NIE + \(c'\);
  • the proportion mediated NIE / TE.

The estimand is the fixed-slope one: the paths do not vary across clusters (no random slopes, so the covariance of the cluster-specific \(a_j\) and \(b_j\) is taken to be zero), and the between effects run through latent cluster means. Nothing is defined across levels, so there is no cross-level total effect and no cross-level proportion mediated. The formulas, the gradients and the cross-level covariance are in the Methods and Formulas article.

Two caveats belong to the estimand, not to the software:

  • Fixed versus random slopes. With random slopes the average indirect effect in the population of clusters is \(ab + \sigma_{ab}\), not \(ab\) (Kenny, Korchmaros and Bolger, 2003; Bauer, Preacher and Gil, 2006). medfit’s number is the fixed-slope \(ab\) and equals the average only when the covariance of the cluster-specific \(a_j\) and \(b_j\) is zero. The adapter does not fit random slopes.
  • Latent versus manifest cluster means. Using latent cluster means (what lavaan’s two-level model does) or observed cluster means is a modeling choice with a causal story attached, not a technicality (Preacher, Zyphur and Zhang, 2010; Lüdtke et al., 2008). Observed means carry sampling error when clusters are small, which biases the between slopes. medfit stores between_parameterization = "latent" and does not offer the manifest alternative.

Fit it and extract it

The data are simulated: 100 clusters of 5 units, a treatment with within and between variance, and known within and between slopes. The model writes the same regressions at both levels.

set.seed(2026)
J <- 100
n <- 5
id <- rep(seq_len(J), each = n)
xb <- rnorm(J)[id]
xw <- rnorm(J * n)
x <- xb + xw
m <- 0.4 * xw + 0.7 * xb + 0.5 * rnorm(J)[id] + rnorm(J * n)
mbar <- ave(m, id)
y <- 0.3 * xw + 0.2 * xb + 0.5 * (m - mbar) + 0.9 * mbar + 0.5 * rnorm(J)[id] + rnorm(J * n)
d <- data.frame(id = id, X = x, M = m, Y = y)

model <- "
  level: 1
    M ~ X
    Y ~ M + X
  level: 2
    M ~ X
    Y ~ M + X
"
fit <- lavaan::sem(model, data = d, cluster = "id")
td <- extract_mediation(fit, treatment = "X", mediator = "M", outcome = "Y")
td
<TwoLevelMediationData>
  X -> M -> Y  (clusters: id; lavaan 0.7.3 fit; between level: latent cluster means)
  n = 500 in 100 clusters (sizes 5 to 5)   |   ICC: X 0.503, M 0.323, Y 0.400
  a_within = +0.4432   b_within = +0.5518   c_prime_within = +0.2685
  a_between = +0.5594   b_between = +0.9553   c_prime_between = +0.2289
  NIE within  (a_within * b_within)   = +0.2446
  NIE between (a_between * b_between) = +0.5344
  Contrast (within - between)         = -0.2899  (descriptive, not a test)

extract_mediation() reads the fit; it never refits. It finds each path by the variable names and the level, not by label, and takes the covariance of the six slopes as the matching sub-block of lavaan’s joint covariance, so the covariance between a within and a between slope is carried into every standard error. The object also stores the intraclass correlation (ICC) of each variable, the cluster sizes, and how the fit was made (fixed_x, the information matrix, the estimator and how missing data were handled).

Read it

nie() takes a level: "within" (the default), "between", "contrast" (within minus between) or "both". nde(), te() and pm() take "within", "between" or "both".

nie(td)
Natural Indirect Effect (NIE): 0.2446
nie(td, level = "between")
Natural Indirect Effect (NIE), between level: 0.5344
nie(td, level = "both")
Natural Indirect Effect (NIE), both levels: within = 0.2446, between = 0.5344
tidy(td, conf_int = TRUE)

tidy() lists the six paths, the four effects at each level, and the contrast. Standard errors come from the delta method over the joint covariance; the intervals are Wald (normal) intervals with no small-sample correction. summary(td) adds the provenance of the fit and prints the assumptions in full, and glance(td) gives one row. The provenance (summary(td)$provenance) records the fitting source, the version of the package that made the fit (source_version; the print() header shows it too) and the estimation settings.

Sample Size: 500 in 100 clusters (sizes 5 to 5)
ICC:         X 0.503, M 0.323, Y 0.400
Fit:         lavaan 0.7.3 (estimator ML, fixed_x TRUE, information observed, h1_information structured, se standard, missing listwise)

Estimand and assumptions:
  Design: treatment `X`, mediator `M` and outcome `Y` measured on level-1 units in 100
    clusters (`id`); the paths are estimated separately at the within and the between
    level.
  - Fixed slopes (no random slopes); between effects are through latent cluster means.
  - Linear paths with no mediator-by-treatment product; no confounding of the paths
    beyond the model.
  - Per level NIE = a * b, NDE = c', TE = NIE + c'; the contrast is within minus
    between NIE.
  - No cross-level total effect or proportion mediated is defined.
  - Intervals are Wald (delta method); there is no small-sample correction.
  - fixed_x is TRUE: the between-path standard errors are conditional on the sample
    between-level moments of the treatment; refit with fixed.x = FALSE for the
    unconditional ones.

Check it against something simple

The within paths are the least-squares slopes on data centered at each cluster’s mean. The maximum-likelihood and least-squares estimates differ slightly, so the two agree closely, not exactly:

dc <- data.frame(Xc = d$X - ave(d$X, d$id), Mc = d$M - ave(d$M, d$id), Yc = d$Y - ave(d$Y, d$id))
ols <- c(a = unname(coef(lm(Mc ~ 0 + Xc, dc))["Xc"]),
         b = unname(coef(lm(Yc ~ 0 + Mc + Xc, dc))["Mc"]),
         c_prime = unname(coef(lm(Yc ~ 0 + Mc + Xc, dc))["Xc"]))
round(rbind(medfit = paths(td)[1:3], ols_on_centered_data = ols), 4)
                     a_within b_within c_prime_within
medfit                 0.4432   0.5518         0.2685
ols_on_centered_data   0.4432   0.5518         0.2685

The between slopes have no such shortcut: a regression on observed cluster means is a different (manifest) model. Compare them with lavaan’s own defined parameters instead:

labeled <- "
  level: 1
    M ~ aw*X
    Y ~ bw*M + cw*X
  level: 2
    M ~ ab*X
    Y ~ bb*M + cb*X
  nie_within := aw*bw
  nie_between := ab*bb
  nie_contrast := aw*bw - ab*bb
"
pe <- lavaan::parameterEstimates(lavaan::sem(labeled, data = d, cluster = "id"))
rbind(lavaan = pe[pe$op == ":=", "se"],
      medfit = tidy(td, type = "effects")$std_error[c(1, 5, 9)])
             [,1]      [,2]      [,3]
lavaan 0.03536782 0.1271784 0.1372484
medfit 0.03536782 0.1271784 0.1372484

The contrast is descriptive

nie(td, level = "contrast") is the within NIE minus the between NIE, with a delta-method standard error. It describes how the two levels differ in this fit. It is not a test: medfit makes no claim that a contrast interval excluding zero shows the levels differ in the population, and no source supports the contrast as a named test. It is returned unless both a and b are equated across levels (see below). decompose(td) returns the within, between and contrast values without a standard error and labels them descriptive.

decompose(td)
    within    between   contrast
 0.2445538  0.5344197 -0.2898659
attr(,"label")
[1] "descriptive; the contrast is not a test"

When the between level is not identified

The between slopes need between-cluster variance in the treatment (for \(a_b\)) and in the mediator (for \(b_b\)). When the ICC of either is below 0.01, a between covariance is not finite, the joint covariance of the paths is not positive definite, or the fit did not converge, the object is within-only: the between properties are NA, the between rows are absent from estimates and vcov, and extraction warns with class medfit_between_unidentified. The between effects and the contrast then return NA with the same warning, never an error and never 0 +/- 0.

The chunk below removes the treatment’s between variance by centering it within clusters (lavaan may warn about the degenerate between level; the warning is lavaan’s, so the fit is wrapped in suppressWarnings()):

d0 <- d
d0$X <- d$X - ave(d$X, d$id)
fit0 <- suppressWarnings(lavaan::sem(model, data = d0, cluster = "id"))
caught <- NULL
td0 <- withCallingHandlers(
  extract_mediation(fit0, treatment = "X", mediator = "M", outcome = "Y"),
  warning = function(w) {
    caught <<- w
    invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
  }
)
class(caught)[1]
[1] "medfit_between_unidentified"
td0@between_identified
[1] FALSE
paths(td0)
       a_within        b_within  c_prime_within       a_between       b_between
      0.4432175       0.5517617       0.2684714              NA              NA
c_prime_between
             NA 
suppressWarnings(nie(td0, level = "between"))
Natural Indirect Effect (NIE), between level: NA

A treatment ICC between 0.01 and 0.05 (or the same for the mediator) keeps the between results and warns with class medfit_warning_between_weak: they may be imprecise. These thresholds, 0.01 and 0.05, are judgments, not published cutoffs; they are the options medfit.between_icc_error and medfit.between_icc_warn.

Which ICC the rule reads

The rule reads the unrestricted (h1) ICC: the between variance over the total in the saturated two-level model, which @icc stores. On the lavaan route it is lavaan::lavInspect(fit, "icc"), with a between-only variable counted as 1; on the native route medfit estimates the same saturated moments by an EM algorithm on the per-size cluster summaries. It is not the ratio the fitted model implies. A fit whose model-implied level-2 variance is negative used to have that ratio clamped to 0 and so came out within-only; its h1 ICC is usually above 0.01, so such a fit is now weak or identified (admissible still reports the negative variance). Within-only is therefore rarer than in earlier development builds.

Two conditions cover the cases where the h1 ICC is missing or not settled. A lavaan fit without an h1 estimate (h1 = FALSE), or a native fit whose summaries cannot give one, uses the model-implied ICC and warns with class medfit_warning_twolevel_icc_h1_unavailable. A native EM that does not converge keeps its last iterate and warns with class medfit_warning_twolevel_icc_h1_unconverged.

The two routes agree on the ICC to about 3e-5 when lavaan’s h1 EM is run to convergence, but lavaan’s default h1 EM stops early. When an ICC sits near 0.01 or 0.05 the routes can then fall on opposite sides of a cut: in about 1 of 50 boundary-heavy simulated datasets we checked, the within-only or weak call differed between the lavaan route and the native route. When an ICC is near a cut, tighten the EM in the lavaan fit with em.h1.args = list(tol = 1e-10, max_iter = 100000L) (lavaan 0.7; lavaan 0.6 takes em.h1.tol = 1e-10 and em.h1.iter.max = 100000), an argument of lavaan::lavaan() and lavaan::sem(). The tolerance alone can stop at the default iteration cap and leave the ICC off the converged value.

Paths equated across levels

If you give the same label to a path at both levels (M ~ a*X in both blocks) or add a == a2, lavaan estimates one parameter for both. The object lists the equated paths in cross_level_equal. medfit finds an equated path three ways: a shared free parameter or label, an == row between the two labels, and a numeric check of the fit itself. The numeric check records a path as equated when the estimated difference of its two level estimates and the variance of that difference are both effectively zero: \(|\hat\theta_w - \hat\theta_b| \le 10^{-6} \max(1, |\hat\theta_w|, |\hat\theta_b|)\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(\hat\theta_w - \hat\theta_b) \le 10^{-10} (V_{ww} + V_{bb})\). Those two defaults are the options medfit.twolevel_equal_diff and medfit.twolevel_equal_var. The check finds an algebraic equality that lavaan keeps as two parameters (for example a^2 - a2^2 == 0). A constant offset between the two levels (a2 == a + 0.01) is a constraint but not an equality, so it is not flagged unless it is smaller than the tolerance, where the paths are equal to that precision. It never uses the correlation of the two estimates: a correlation of \(-1\), or of \(+1\) between proportional but unequal paths, does not mean the paths are equal, and the contrast would silently become NA.

The contrast follows the equated paths. With only one of a or b equated, the contrast stays an estimate: with a equated it is \(a (b_w - b_b)\), with b equated it is \((a_w - a_b) b\), each with a delta-method standard error from the joint covariance (the cross-level covariance of the equated pair enters the gradient). It is still descriptive, not a test. Only when both a and b are equated is the contrast zero by constraint, not an estimate: it is NA and carries the warning medfit_warning_twolevel_constrained. The chunk below checks the a-only contrast and its standard error against lavaan’s own := definition.

shared <- "
  level: 1
    M ~ a*X
    Y ~ b*M + X
  level: 2
    M ~ a*X
    Y ~ b2*M + X
  nc := a*b - a*b2
"
fit_eq <- suppressWarnings(lavaan::sem(shared, data = d, cluster = "id"))
td_eq <- extract_mediation(fit_eq, treatment = "X", mediator = "M", outcome = "Y")
td_eq@cross_level_equal
[1] "a"
eff_eq <- tidy(td_eq, type = "effects")
eff_eq[eff_eq$term == "nie_contrast", ]
# A tibble: 1 × 3
  term         estimate std_error
  <chr>           <dbl>     <dbl>
1 nie_contrast   -0.199     0.102
pe_eq <- lavaan::parameterEstimates(fit_eq)
pe_eq[pe_eq$op == ":=", c("est", "se")]
      est    se
19 -0.199 0.102
nie(td_eq, level = "between")
Natural Indirect Effect (NIE), between level: 0.4644

With both equated, the contrast is NA and twolevel_statistic() refuses it.

shared_ab <- "
  level: 1
    M ~ a*X
    Y ~ b*M + X
  level: 2
    M ~ a*X
    Y ~ b*M + X
"
fit_eq2 <- suppressWarnings(lavaan::sem(shared_ab, data = d, cluster = "id"))
td_eq2 <- extract_mediation(fit_eq2, treatment = "X", mediator = "M", outcome = "Y")
td_eq2@cross_level_equal
[1] "a" "b"
suppressWarnings(nie(td_eq2, level = "contrast"))
Natural Indirect Effect (NIE), within - between contrast: NA

Few clusters

extract_mediation() warns, and never errors, when the fit has fewer than 50 clusters (class medfit_warning_twolevel_few_clusters), on both routes. The 50 is a judgment: no source gives a cluster count below which two-level estimates or between-level standard errors are trustworthy. The threshold is editable with options(medfit.twolevel_min_clusters = ).

With few clusters the between-level results are unreliable, and the within-level results are less affected. Treat the warning, and medfit_warning_between_weak (an ICC below 0.05), as the signal that the between interval may be missing, wide or too narrow; the troubleshooting guide lists both.

The guidance below comes from a simulation study of the lavaan two-level adapter, fitted with delta-method and Monte Carlo intervals and the settings medfit ships. It did not run the cluster bootstrap beyond a small pilot, so it says nothing about how well that bootstrap performs with few clusters. A fit counts as a failure when lavaan errors, does not converge or the adapter errors. The study used 5 or 20 units per cluster and 10 to 100 clusters, and ran before the within-only rule moved to the unrestricted ICC.

  • Equal cluster sizes failed in at most .18 of fits at any number of clusters in the grid. With 5 units per cluster and an ICC of 0.05 the rate stayed above .05 at every number of clusters tried (.097 at 50, .059 at 100).
  • Unequal cluster sizes failed far more often, most of all with 5 units per cluster and an ICC of 0.05: .93 of fits at 10 clusters, .31 at 50 and .06 at 100. Failure first fell below .20 for every ICC studied only at 100 clusters, the largest number tried. Unequal clusters of 5 units therefore fail often even with 50 clusters when the ICC is low.
  • The within indirect effect covered near the nominal level in the fits that returned an interval (median .94 to .95 at every number of clusters tried). Its overall coverage fell short because failed fits return no interval.
  • The between indirect effect is the weak spot. With an ICC of 0.05 and 100 clusters its coverage was about .81 (median over the cells), because the between interval was available in only about .69 of fits: the rest were within-only, failed or inadmissible. More clusters did not remove that.

These are simulation results for a few designs, not guarantees. With fewer than about 50 clusters, and especially with unequal sizes, report the between-level results as exploratory.

Standard errors under fixed.x = TRUE

lavaan’s sem() fixes the exogenous variables at their sample values by default (fixed.x = TRUE), and the object records this as fixed_x. Under it the between-path standard errors are conditional on the sample between-level moments of the treatment; refit with fixed.x = FALSE for the unconditional ones. medfit reads the standard errors lavaan reports and does not adjust them; summary() prints a note when fixed_x is TRUE.

The sem engine route

medfit’s own maximum-likelihood SEM engine (the sem engine) fits the same model from the same level: syntax, without lavaan: give fit_sem() the cluster column. This route is experimental, and new in the development version. level: 1 and level: within name the within block; level: 2, level: between and the cluster column’s name name the between block.

nfit <- fit_sem(model, data = d, cluster = "id")
ntd <- extract_mediation(nfit, treatment = "X", mediator = "M", outcome = "Y")
ntd
<TwoLevelMediationData>
  X -> M -> Y  (clusters: id; native 0.21.3 fit; between level: latent cluster means)
  n = 500 in 100 clusters (sizes 5 to 5)   |   ICC: X 0.503, M 0.323, Y 0.400
  a_within = +0.4432   b_within = +0.5518   c_prime_within = +0.2685
  a_between = +0.5595   b_between = +0.9553   c_prime_between = +0.2289
  NIE within  (a_within * b_within)   = +0.2446
  NIE between (a_between * b_between) = +0.5344
  Contrast (within - between)         = -0.2899  (descriptive, not a test)
ntd@source
[1] "native"

extract_mediation() returns the same TwoLevelMediationData as the lavaan route, with @source set to "native", so nie(), tidy(), decompose() and the bootstrap work on it unchanged. The engine fits every exogenous variable’s moments (the fixed.x = FALSE setting; an explicit fixed_x = TRUE is refused) and uses the observed information. It matches lavaan fitted with fixed.x = FALSE, information = "observed", h1.information = "structured":

lfit <- lavaan::sem(model, data = d, cluster = "id", fixed.x = FALSE, information = "observed",
                    h1.information = "structured")
ltd <- extract_mediation(lfit, treatment = "X", mediator = "M", outcome = "Y")
cbind(native = coef(ntd), lavaan = coef(ltd))
                   native    lavaan
a_within        0.4432190 0.4432169
b_within        0.5517596 0.5517596
c_prime_within  0.2684745 0.2684742
a_between       0.5594504 0.5594438
b_between       0.9552588 0.9552714
c_prime_between 0.2289369 0.2289345
cbind(native = sqrt(diag(ntd@vcov)), lavaan = sqrt(diag(ltd@vcov)))
                    native     lavaan
a_within        0.04954385 0.04954396
b_within        0.05063172 0.05063169
c_prime_within  0.05496003 0.05496000
a_between       0.07326930 0.07326872
b_between       0.19402040 0.19402385
c_prime_between 0.13375489 0.13375574

The standard errors agree as well. The between-path standard errors of the default lavaan fit in Fit it and extract it are slightly different, because that fit uses fixed.x = TRUE (Standard errors under fixed.x = TRUE).

glance() on the fit reports the cluster count and the range of cluster sizes, counted after incomplete rows are dropped. The chi-square test and its p-value are NA, with a note, because the engine fits no saturated two-level model; df and the log likelihood (of both levels together) are reported.

glance(nfit)[, c("nobs", "n_clusters", "cluster_size_min", "cluster_size_max", "df", "logLik", "chisq")]
# A tibble: 1 × 7
   nobs n_clusters cluster_size_min cluster_size_max    df logLik chisq
  <int>      <int>            <int>            <int> <int>  <dbl> <dbl>
1   500        100                5                5     0 -2287.    NA

Level-2 variances are fitted without a floor, so a between-level variance can come out negative, most often with few or small clusters. The engine then stops with class medfit_error_twolevel_inadmissible rather than return the solution; the condition carries the fit (fit) and the outcome ledger (ledger), whose admissibility entry gives the verdict and the reasons per level. The data below have 30 clusters of 3 and a small between-level variance of the mediator and the outcome:

d_neg <- withr::with_seed(1, {
  n_neg <- 30
  cl <- sort(rep(seq_len(n_neg), 3))
  xb <- rnorm(n_neg)
  mb <- 0.5 * xb + rnorm(n_neg, sd = 0.3)
  yb <- 0.3 * mb + 0.2 * xb
  x <- xb[cl] + rnorm(length(cl))
  m <- mb[cl] + 0.4 * x + rnorm(length(cl))
  y <- yb[cl] + 0.3 * m + 0.2 * x + rnorm(length(cl), sd = 1.5)
  data.frame(id = cl, X = x, M = m, Y = y)
})

err <- tryCatch(fit_sem(model, data = d_neg, cluster = "id"), error = function(e) e)
class(err)[1]
[1] "medfit_error_twolevel_inadmissible"
conditionMessage(err)
[1] "the two-level solution is inadmissible: negative level-2 variance: M~~M.l2, Y~~Y.l2; the implied between covariance Sigma_B is not positive definite. Level-2 variances are fitted without a floor (experimental); the fit is kept in the condition (`fit`) as evidence"
err$ledger$admissibility$between$reasons
[1] "negative level-2 variance: M~~M.l2, Y~~Y.l2"
[2] "the implied between covariance Sigma_B is not positive definite"

The lavaan route on the same data returns the estimates with the warning medfit_warning_twolevel_inadmissible instead. The sem engine route refuses latent variables, product terms, weights, missing = "fiml", nonlinear constraints, fixed_x = TRUE, meanstructure = FALSE, information = "expected" and a variable named only in level: 1 rows, each with a classed error whose name starts medfit_error_twolevel_; the full table of messages is in the “Two-level models” section of ?"medfit-syntax". A labeled path, a linear equality across levels and a variable named only in level: 2 rows (constant within each cluster) are accepted.

Cluster-robust standard errors

se_type = "sandwich" on a two-level fit gives cluster-robust standard errors: the sandwich \(A^{-1} B A^{-1}\) with the observed information as \(A\) and \(B = \sum_j s_j s_j'\) summed over the per-cluster scores \(s_j\), with no small-sample factor (CR0). Under an active linear constraint, such as a path equated across levels, the sandwich is projected onto the constraint, as in a single-level fit. The estimates are the same as with the default se_type = "model"; only the covariance changes. It matches lavaan’s se = "robust.huber.white" for the same model:

nfit_r <- fit_sem(model, data = d, cluster = "id", se_type = "sandwich")
ntd_r <- extract_mediation(nfit_r, treatment = "X", mediator = "M", outcome = "Y")
lfit_r <- lavaan::sem(model, data = d, cluster = "id", fixed.x = FALSE, information = "observed",
                      h1.information = "structured", se = "robust.huber.white")
ltd_r <- extract_mediation(lfit_r, treatment = "X", mediator = "M", outcome = "Y")
cbind(model = sqrt(diag(ntd@vcov)), sandwich = sqrt(diag(ntd_r@vcov)), lavaan = sqrt(diag(ltd_r@vcov)))
                     model   sandwich     lavaan
a_within        0.04954385 0.04901290 0.04901297
b_within        0.05063172 0.05359923 0.05359928
c_prime_within  0.05496003 0.05498679 0.05498685
a_between       0.07326930 0.07204548 0.07204560
b_between       0.19402040 0.20326265 0.20326800
c_prime_between 0.13375489 0.13829954 0.13830160

print() and summary() of the fit name the standard errors as cluster-robust with the number of clusters, and glance() reports se_type. The intervals of confint() and tidy() use the normal reference, and the few-clusters warning still applies: the cluster sandwich is biased downward with few clusters, and medfit adds no small-sample correction. Sampling weights, product terms, nonlinear constraints and information = "expected" stay refused with se_type = "sandwich" as with the default.

Bootstrap

twolevel_statistic() turns one two-level effect into the scalar statistic that bootstrap_mediation() needs. The effect is "nie_within", "nie_between", "nie_contrast", the other per-level effects ("nde_*", "te_*", "pm_*") or one of the six paths. The first argument decides the route:

  • Parametric (and "plugin"): pass the TwoLevelMediationData. Each draw comes from the normal distribution of the six paths with their joint covariance, so the cross-level covariance is part of every draw. This is fast and has the same normality assumption as the delta method.
  • Cluster (nonparametric): pass the lavaan fit and the roles (treatment, mediator, outcome), and give bootstrap_mediation() the data and cluster =. Each replicate resamples whole clusters and refits the model stored in the fit’s own call, with only the standard errors, the model test and lavaan’s post-check switched off (se = "none", test = "none", check.post = FALSE; none changes the point estimates). A cluster drawn twice is refitted as two clusters.
b_par <- bootstrap_mediation(
  twolevel_statistic(td, "nie_between"),
  method = "parametric", mediation_data = td, n_boot = 1000, seed = 1
)
b_par
BootstrapResult object
======================

Method:   parametric
Estimate:   0.5344
N bootstrap samples: 1000

95% Confidence Interval:
  Lower:   0.2901
  Upper:   0.8234
b_cl <- bootstrap_mediation(
  twolevel_statistic(fit, "nie_between", treatment = "X", mediator = "M", outcome = "Y"),
  method = "nonparametric", data = d, cluster = "id", n_boot = 30, seed = 1
)
c(estimate = b_cl@estimate, n_boot = b_cl@n_boot)
  estimate     n_boot
 0.5344197 30.0000000

Both routes report the point estimate of the original fit, which equals nie(td, level = "between"). The cluster call here uses 30 replicates only to keep the page fast; use at least several hundred for an interval.

Three things to know about the cluster route:

  • Report the percentile interval, not the standard deviation. Refits that are inadmissible (for example, a negative between variance) are kept, because the point estimate keeps them too and the percentile interval is defined on the same footing. At a few dozen clusters such boundary refits give the between effects and the contrast heavy tails, so the plain standard deviation of the draws can exceed the delta standard error while the percentile interval stays close to it. Use ci_lower and ci_upper and do not treat the standard deviation of boot_estimates as a standard error.
  • Failed replicates are counted. A refit that errors, warns, does not converge, or leaves the between level unidentified in that resample (an ICC below medfit.between_icc_error) is excluded and the count is reported in a warning (bootstrap samples failed and were excluded); n_boot in the result is the number of replicates that were used.
  • Constructing the callback can fail. A between effect or the contrast of a within-only fit stops with class medfit_between_unidentified, and the contrast of a fit that equates both a and b across levels stops with class medfit_error_twolevel_constrained, instead of bootstrapping a distribution of NA. A lavaan fit without treatment, mediator and outcome stops with class medfit_error_twolevel_unsupported.
err_within_only <- tryCatch(
  twolevel_statistic(td0, "nie_between"),
  medfit_between_unidentified = function(e) class(e)[1]
)
err_constrained <- tryCatch(
  twolevel_statistic(td_eq2, "nie_contrast"),
  medfit_error_twolevel_constrained = function(e) class(e)[1]
)
c(err_within_only, err_constrained)
[1] "medfit_between_unidentified"       "medfit_error_twolevel_constrained"

Passing an object to bootstrap_mediation() and having it choose the cluster route by itself is not available; the two calls above are the supported ones.

Several parallel mediators

With two or more mediators, none regressed on another, extract_mediation() returns the experimental TwoLevelParallelMediationData. Each mediator has its own a and b path at each level, and the effects come per level as for one mediator. nie() adds type: "total" (the default) is the sum of the specific effects, and "specific" gives one value per mediator. The contrast is again within minus between and descriptive. A mediator’s contrast is NA only when both its a and its b are equated across levels, and the total contrast only when that holds for every mediator. The formulas and gradients are in the Methods and Formulas article.

set.seed(2027)
id_k <- rep(seq_len(100), each = 5)
xb_k <- rnorm(100)[id_k]
xw_k <- rnorm(500)
m1 <- 0.4 * xw_k + 0.7 * xb_k + 0.5 * rnorm(100)[id_k] + rnorm(500)
m2 <- 0.3 * xw_k + 0.5 * xb_k + 0.5 * rnorm(100)[id_k] + rnorm(500)
y_k <- 0.3 * xw_k + 0.2 * xb_k + 0.5 * (m1 - ave(m1, id_k)) + 0.9 * ave(m1, id_k) +
  0.4 * (m2 - ave(m2, id_k)) + 0.6 * ave(m2, id_k) + 0.5 * rnorm(100)[id_k] + rnorm(500)
d_k <- data.frame(id = id_k, X = xb_k + xw_k, M1 = m1, M2 = m2, Y = y_k)
model_k <- "
  level: 1
    M1 ~ X
    M2 ~ X
    Y ~ M1 + M2 + X
  level: 2
    M1 ~ X
    M2 ~ X
    Y ~ M1 + M2 + X
"
fit_k <- lavaan::sem(model_k, data = d_k, cluster = "id")
tk <- extract_mediation(fit_k, treatment = "X", mediator = c("M1", "M2"), outcome = "Y")
nie(tk, level = "both")
Natural Indirect Effect (NIE), both levels: within = 0.3794, between = 1.4093
nie(tk, type = "specific")
Natural Indirect Effect (NIE): M1 = 0.2294, M2 = 0.1499
nie(tk, level = "contrast", type = "specific")
Natural Indirect Effect (NIE), within - between contrast: M1 = -0.5667, M2 = -0.4632
decompose(tk)
         within   between   contrast
M1    0.2294339 0.7961111 -0.5666772
M2    0.1499245 0.6131525 -0.4632281
total 0.3793584 1.4092637 -1.0299053
attr(,"label")
[1] "descriptive; the contrast is not a test"
tidy(tk, type = "effects")
# A tibble: 15 × 3
   term            estimate std_error
   <chr>              <dbl>     <dbl>
 1 nie_M1_within      0.229    0.0359
 2 nie_M2_within      0.150    0.0277
 3 nie_within         0.379    0.0451

tidy() lists each specific effect, the total, NDE, TE and PM at each level, then the specific and total contrasts. The standard errors use the joint covariance of all the paths, so the covariance between two mediators’ paths enters the standard error of the total. Here @vcov carries the covariance of a_M1 and a_M2, which the lm/glm ParallelMediationData leaves out. The between level is kept only when the ICC of the treatment and of every mediator is at least 0.01; one mediator without a between part makes the whole result within-only (medfit_between_unidentified).

Check it against lavaan

paths() names each path by mediator and level. Label the same model and define the effects with :=; the estimates and standard errors match tidy():

paths(tk)
    a_M1_within     a_M2_within     b_M1_within     b_M2_within  c_prime_within
      0.3867350       0.3482710       0.5932587       0.4304822       0.2552809
   a_M1_between    a_M2_between    b_M1_between    b_M2_between c_prime_between
      0.6936137       0.5418557       1.1477732       1.1315790      -0.2008242 
labeled_k <- "
  level: 1
    M1 ~ a1w*X
    M2 ~ a2w*X
    Y ~ b1w*M1 + b2w*M2 + cw*X
  level: 2
    M1 ~ a1b*X
    M2 ~ a2b*X
    Y ~ b1b*M1 + b2b*M2 + cb*X
  nie_M1_within := a1w*b1w
  nie_within := a1w*b1w + a2w*b2w
  nie_between := a1b*b1b + a2b*b2b
  nie_contrast := (a1w*b1w + a2w*b2w) - (a1b*b1b + a2b*b2b)
"
pe_k <- lavaan::parameterEstimates(lavaan::sem(labeled_k, data = d_k, cluster = "id"))
pe_k <- pe_k[pe_k$op == ":=", ]
tidy_k <- tidy(tk, type = "effects")
tidy_k <- tidy_k[match(pe_k$lhs, tidy_k$term), ]
round(cbind(lavaan_est = pe_k$est, medfit_est = tidy_k$estimate,
            lavaan_se = pe_k$se, medfit_se = tidy_k$std_error), 5)
     lavaan_est medfit_est lavaan_se medfit_se
[1,]    0.22943    0.22943   0.03594   0.03594
[2,]    0.37936    0.37936   0.04512   0.04512
[3,]    1.40926    1.40926   0.24362   0.24362
[4,]   -1.02991   -1.02991   0.25438   0.25438

One mediator’s paths equated across levels

When both a and b of one mediator carry the same label at the two levels, that mediator’s contrast is zero by constraint and is NA, with the warning medfit_warning_twolevel_constrained. The other mediator’s contrast and the total contrast are still returned (lavaan warns that level-specific fit measures are not available with cross-level constraints; that warning is lavaan’s, so the fit is wrapped in suppressWarnings()):

model_k_eq <- "
  level: 1
    M1 ~ a1*X
    M2 ~ X
    Y ~ b1*M1 + M2 + X
  level: 2
    M1 ~ a1*X
    M2 ~ X
    Y ~ b1*M1 + M2 + X
"
fit_k_eq <- suppressWarnings(lavaan::sem(model_k_eq, data = d_k, cluster = "id"))
tk_eq <- extract_mediation(fit_k_eq, treatment = "X", mediator = c("M1", "M2"), outcome = "Y")
nie(tk_eq, level = "contrast", type = "specific")
Warning: The contrast NIE_within - NIE_between is NA for nie_M1_contrast: both
a and b of the mediator are equated across levels, so the contrast is zero by
constraint. The within and between effects are still reported.
Natural Indirect Effect (NIE), within - between contrast: M1 =      NA, M2 = -0.4251
nie(tk_eq, level = "contrast")
Natural Indirect Effect (NIE), within - between contrast: -0.4251

The total contrast equals the M2 contrast here, because the M1 part is zero by constraint.

twolevel_statistic() builds the bootstrap callback for several mediators too. effect is "nie" (the total, the default), "nie_j" (the specific effect of the mediator named in specific), "nde" or "te", and level is "within" (the default), "between" or "contrast" (within minus between, for "nie" and "nie_j" only). Pass the object for the parametric bootstrap:

b_k <- bootstrap_mediation(
  twolevel_statistic(tk, "nie", level = "between"),
  method = "parametric", mediation_data = tk, n_boot = 200, seed = 1
)
b_k_m1 <- bootstrap_mediation(
  twolevel_statistic(tk, "nie_j", specific = "M1"),
  method = "parametric", mediation_data = tk, n_boot = 200, seed = 1
)
rbind(
  total_between = c(estimate = b_k@estimate, lower = b_k@ci_lower, upper = b_k@ci_upper),
  M1_within = c(estimate = b_k_m1@estimate, lower = b_k_m1@ci_lower, upper = b_k_m1@ci_upper)
)
               estimate     lower     upper
total_between 1.4092637 1.0077536 1.9359104
M1_within     0.2294339 0.1584271 0.3057644

For the cluster bootstrap, pass the lavaan fit with all the mediators, as in twolevel_statistic(fit_k, "nie", level = "between", treatment = "X", mediator = c("M1", "M2"), outcome = "Y"), and give bootstrap_mediation() the data and cluster =, as for one mediator. A refit’s between level counts as identified only when the treatment and every mediator pass the ICC check. An invalid level, or a contrast asked of "nde" or "te", stops with class medfit_error_twolevel_level; an unknown effect or a missing or unknown specific stops with class medfit_error_twolevel_unsupported.

Testing the indirect effect at one level

mbco_sem() tests the indirect effect at one level of a sem engine fit. It needs labeled paths, so the model below labels them at each level. Each null refits the model with one path set to 0, on both levels and with the same clusters; the statistic is the smaller of the likelihood ratios, referred to chi-square(1) (Methods and Formulas). The result adds level and n_clusters.

model_lab <- "
  level: 1
    M ~ a_w*X
    Y ~ b_w*M + X
  level: 2
    M ~ a_b*X
    Y ~ b_b*M + X
"
nfit_lab <- fit_sem(model_lab, data = d, cluster = "id")
mbco_between <- mbco_sem(nfit_lab, "a_b", "b_b")
mbco_between

    Minimum-of-two likelihood-ratio tests (MBCO) for an indirect effect

data:  a_b * b_b = 0
MBCO = 19.729, df = 1, p-value = 8.924e-06
mbco_between$level
[1] "between"
mbco_between$n_clusters
[1] 100

mbco_sem(nfit_lab, "a_w", "b_w") tests the within indirect effect the same way. On these data the refit with b_w == 0 gives the outcome a negative level-2 variance, so that null solution is inadmissible: the result is unresolved (statistic NA), with a warning of class medfit_warning_twolevel_inadmissible that names the refit, and $tests shows which null failed. The statistic is not taken from the other null alone:

mbco_within <- mbco_sem(nfit_lab, "a_w", "b_w")
Warning: the refit with `b_w == 0` converged to an inadmissible solution (negative level-2 variance: Y~~Y.l2; the implied between covariance Sigma_B is not positive definite).
The MBCO statistic is not available (NA); `$tests` lists each refit.
mbco_within$unresolved
[1] TRUE
mbco_within$tests[, c("constraint", "converged")]
  constraint converged
1   a_w == 0      TRUE
2   b_w == 0     FALSE

The test is conservative when both paths are zero, and it is not a test of the between-minus-within contrast, which stays descriptive (The contrast is descriptive). Paths from different levels (mbco_sem(fit, "a_w", "b_b")) stop with class medfit_error_twolevel_unsupported. A null refit with an inadmissible solution gives statistic NA with the warning medfit_warning_twolevel_inadmissible; one that does not converge gives statistic NA with a warning. A warning also flags a level-2 variance below 0.01 of its implied between plus within variance at a refit, where chi-square(1) may not hold. compare_lr() is not available for a two-level fit yet. A test that the two levels’ indirect effects are equal is a separate function, twolevel_equal_indirect(fit): the likelihood ratio of the free fit against the fit with a_w*b_w == a_b*b_b, referred to chi-square(1) (singular where all four paths are 0, and asymptotic in the number of clusters; n_boot gives a parametric bootstrap p-value for few clusters; replications whose refit is not admissible are dropped and counted in boot$n_dropped, so that p-value is conditional on admissible refits). The constrained surface has sign twins (flipping the signs of the within pair, the between pair or both keeps the equality), which are worse optima of the same constraint: the optimizer’s starts-disagree warning is not raised when every disagreeing start is such a twin, and the best start is kept. The twins of the kept fit are also tried from its estimates (a twin certificate): up to three single-start local solves at every n_starts, a twin refit that fails is skipped, and the result is not a proof of a global optimum. A worse twin is therefore not kept with n_starts = 1; a twin that ends inadmissible below the kept fit (a level-2 variance on its boundary) or with a covariance that is not positive definite makes the result unresolved, as it does with more starts. The row allows eight sign patterns; the certificate flips pairs together and reaches the four of the kept fit’s orbit. The other orbit does hold local optima (30 of 35 small cells, closest gap 0.02 LR), and the kept orbit still won every time tested (evidence, not a proof). The result’s twin element records what the certificate did (tried, replaced, flipped, f_gain, unresolved); flipped is read from the signs of the adopted fit against the kept fit’s: "within" or "between" when both paths of that pair changed sign, "other" once for any other sign change (including a path that reaches or leaves zero), and empty when no sign changed. It costs about 3 to 4 times the time at n_starts = 1, about twice at the default and about 1.3 times at 30 starts; n_boot p-values for a given seed can differ from 0.19.0. A constrained fit that is inadmissible, not positive definite or not converged gives an unresolved result (statistic NA) with a warning, never a number. The descriptive contrast carries no p-value.

Limits

  • One mediator or several parallel ones, linear paths, observed variables. Two or more mediators return the experimental TwoLevelParallelMediationData (Several parallel mediators); a mediator regressed on another mediator (serial) stops extraction with class medfit_error_twolevel_unsupported. Latent variables and non-Gaussian outcomes are not part of this adapter.
  • No standardized = TRUE. A standardized two-level path mixes the within and the between variances; extraction stops with class medfit_error_twolevel_standardized.
  • No product terms. A : term in a regression, or interaction =, stops extraction with class medfit_error_twolevel_product.
  • No random slopes. See the estimand above.
  • The sem engine route has its own refusals (latent variables, products, weights, FIML and more); see The sem engine route.
  • Three-level and multigroup fits are refused, with classes medfit_error_lavaan_multilevel and medfit_error_lavaan_multigroup.
  • The treatment and the mediator must be in the model at both levels. A treatment assigned to whole clusters is a 2-1-1 design and is fitted with fit_mediation(engine = "lmer", cluster = ); the error is class medfit_error_twolevel_unsupported.
  • Each path must appear once at each level (M ~ X, Y ~ M, Y ~ X). A path that is absent at a level is not assumed to be 0; the error is class medfit_error_twolevel_path_missing.
  • level = "contrast" belongs to nie() only. nde(), te() and pm() refuse it (class medfit_error_twolevel_level); use tidy() for those contrasts.

Conditions it can signal

Each class is a condition class, so tryCatch() and withCallingHandlers() can target one. A warning that you have decided to accept can be muffled by class (see Troubleshooting).

Class Kind When
medfit_between_unidentified warning (error from twolevel_statistic()) the between level is not identified: the result is within-only. Also from a between accessor on a within-only object; twolevel_statistic() stops with this class for a between effect or the contrast
medfit_warning_between_weak warning the ICC of the treatment or of a mediator is in [0.01, 0.05)
medfit_warning_twolevel_icc_h1_unavailable warning no h1 ICC (a lavaan fit with h1 = FALSE, or native summaries too thin or collinear): the model-implied ICC is used for the within-only rule
medfit_warning_twolevel_icc_h1_unconverged warning native route: the EM for the h1 ICC did not converge; its last iterate is used
medfit_warning_twolevel_constrained warning the contrast is NA because both a and b are equated across levels (with several mediators, those of that mediator, or of every mediator for the total)
medfit_warning_twolevel_inadmissible warning lavaan’s post.check is FALSE (for example a negative variance)
medfit_warning_twolevel_few_clusters warning fewer than 50 clusters
medfit_error_twolevel_inadmissible error sem engine route only: a negative level-2 variance or a non-positive-definite implied covariance at either level. Level-2 variances are fitted without a floor; the condition carries the fit (fit) and the ledger (ledger). Its message is shown in The sem engine route
medfit_warning_twolevel_labels_ignored warning a_label, b_label or cp_label was set: the paths are read by variable names and level, not by label
medfit_error_twolevel_standardized error standardized = TRUE
medfit_error_twolevel_product error a product term or interaction =
medfit_error_twolevel_unsupported error a mediator regressed on another mediator (serial), a covariate passed as a mediator, a duplicate or overlapping role, a variable missing at a level (2-1-1), or an argument that does not apply
medfit_error_twolevel_path_missing error a, b or c’ absent at a level
medfit_error_twolevel_unusable error the within block is unusable: the fit did not converge, or the within covariance is missing or not positive definite
medfit_error_twolevel_level error level = "contrast" for nde(), te() or pm(); from twolevel_statistic() with several mediators, an invalid level or level = "contrast" with "nde" or "te"
medfit_error_twolevel_constrained error twolevel_statistic(effect = "nie_contrast") for a fit that equates both a and b across levels; with several mediators, level = "contrast" when both a and b of the mediator ("nie_j") or of every mediator ("nie") are equated

The messages they carry are quoted in Troubleshooting.
